_comment: Template. Copy to projects.json and point paths at THIS machine. Managed with `spear-corpus add/list/rm`. kind is a free label (it scopes skills and prints in the listing). What a corpus DOES is declared separately: indexer (buildsystem|generic), autoindex (build a missing index on sight), prompt_file (a domain prompt for this corpus), collection (name an existing index). Optional per-project keys: exclude (dir names skipped at indexing), include_build, corpora (federate these registered corpora into the session), shared (attach this corpus to EVERY session), collection (name the chroma collection instead of deriving it from the absolute path -- required when the index travels with the registry, as in the container), bench, and the command lists the harness runs to check its own work: build_commands, test_commands, lint_commands, acceptance_commands. A path is either ABSOLUTE (a tree of yours, genuinely machine-specific) or RELATIVE, in which case it is resolved against SPEAR_CORPUS_ROOT -- which defaults to the repository root, so a corpus living inside the repo is found wherever the repo is cloned. A container sets it to its mount root.

infrabase._comment: a build-system tree that VENDORS its components, and the lesson is GRANULARITY. Excluding './linux' wholesale looks right -- 3 GB of fetched kernel under it -- but infrabase TRACKS 43 files in there: the br2-external skeleton with its .its files, and the userspace sources under linux/usr. Measured on the real tree, the wholesale exclude yields 197 indexable files and 13 .its for a 42 GB build system; excluding the fetched and built subtrees one level down instead yields 3037 and 19. Same cap, fifteen times the corpus. Two things are already handled and need no entry here: '.back' snapshots are skipped by suffix wherever they appear, and include_build drops build/{tmp,sstate-cache,downloads,cache,deploy} by itself -- './build/bitbake' below is bitbake's own source, which that list does not cover. './linux/rootfs.0' does need saying: the indexer deliberately does not treat '.0' as a snapshot suffix, because it collides with version directories. Finally the leading ./ matters: linux, qemu, u-boot, so3 and avz occur again as recipe directories under build/meta-*, which carry the recipes and ITS files this corpus exists for -- a bare name would take those with the vendored source.

ib_so3._comment: the ib_ prefix is a CONVENTION, not a feature: a vendored checkout indexed in its own right, named so it cannot be confused with the upstream corpus of the same project. infrabase/so3 and the so3 corpus above are different versions -- the product BSP pins its own -- and answering from the wrong one is the failure this prevents. Sized to fit: 32k files, under the 60k cap that indexing now treats as an error rather than a warning. infrabase/linux (109k) and infrabase/qemu (81k) do NOT fit, and both already have upstream corpora, so they stay excluded rather than prefixed.

lvgl._comment: shows the command lists: what the harness runs to verify a change it made

llama.cpp-next._comment: inside the repository: relative, so a clone anywhere finds it
